description: The .bep file hosts two distinct data categories: versioned plan data and immutable curated artifacts.
High-write-frequency or randomly-accessed data lives outside the .bep for operational use; it may still be included as an immutable archival snapshot.
baseline/ must always be a full structural mirror of the .bep root for any collection with a lifecycle distinct from the plan.
Each operation (commit, discard, reset, squash) does exactly what its target specifies, with no implicit side effects on other targets.
Version history is stored as inverse diffs applied backward from the current state, so bep.json always reflects the latest version at zero reconstruction cost.
BEPs are versioned as two numbers, {major}.{minor} — minor for in-progress patches, major for significant milestones.
Relationships between schema entities are expressed via ID references, never by nesting the referenced entity inline.
Schema keys are always fully spelled out, never abbreviated, so they are legible without external documentation.
Data that can be derived deterministically from existing schema entities is computed on demand, never persisted as its own field or entity.
The format includes constructs designed for direct LLM authorship and consumption (skills, memories, flags), each using the representation natural to that purpose.
Memory IDs are human-readable kebab-case slugs, not UUIDs, so references are legible directly in markdown and filenames.
Runtime handlers get this.bep as a structuredClone() typed Readonly<BEP> — never the authoring Entity API — so the plan can only ever be modified through the platform's own commit/discard operations.
process nodes may have at most one outgoing edge, matching the rule automation already enforced — all branching must go through a decision node, checked in FlowDiagramSchema's superRefine.
Event payload schemas are a minimum contract (what's guaranteed present), not a closed one — validatePayload() never rejects or strips fields an automation/event includes beyond what's declared.

informationDomains/referenceData model structured, domain-organized facts (status enums, CDE folder structures) for external integrations — stored flat with parentId, key unique per-sibling only, reconstructed into a nested object on demand by InformationDomains.resolve(). Each node has a required human-readable label (key is the technical/structural identifier, not meant for display). Live references use JSONata expressions wrapped in {{ }}, evaluated against the raw BEP object as root context.

{{<JSONata expression>}} marks an inline reference inside a standard's markdown prose, reusing the same reference grammar used in referenceData.data; Standards.getResolvedContent() returns plain resolved text for consumers that don't need to render — a UI needing to visually mark references resolves {{...}} itself.

A {{...}} reference is never validated at write time, since JSONata's evaluate() is always async and Entity.add()/.update() are synchronous across the ecosystem; a reference that doesn't resolve is only ever caught on read, as a visible marker. Deletion-block detection (referencesEntity) stays synchronous because it only parses a reference's syntax, never evaluates it.
